title: When the Hollow Burns
premise: Astrid Lockridge has spent twenty-three years in Hollowvale, a valley warded so thoroughly that magic dies at its borders — the perfect hiding place for a beast-speaker whose gift is punishable by burning. When a feral child arrives speaking the Old Tongue and carrying a stolen fragment of a soul, Astrid learns the child's sister was sold to the Undercourt beneath the mountain, and the fragment is a beacon the court's soul-hunters can follow. Fleeing the valley with the child, Astrid bargains with outlaws, river-gods, and a disgraced court scribe, discovering that her gift was not a curse but an inheritance: her mother sold her own soul to buy Astrid's silence and safety. In the end, Astrid stands before the Undercourt's throne and offers a trade — the fragment, her mother's debt, and her own voice — but the child, who has been learning Astrid's language all along, speaks the binding words first, freeing the sister and shattering the court's claim over every soul it holds. Astrid returns voiceless to Hollowvale, only to find the beasts now speak for her, and the valley's ward, fed by her mother's sacrifice, finally lets her go.
about_author: Paloma Underhill is the pen name of a former farrier's apprentice who grew up in a valley town and swears the ravens there held grudges. They write about bargains, borders, and the people who pay for other people's survival.

chapters.title: The Valley That Swallows Magic
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Establishes Hollowvale, her secret gift, and her careful, small life tending animals. She speaks with a dying ewe the way she speaks to no person. Emotional beat: the ache of a life built on concealment.

chapters.title: A Knock at Dusk
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A mud-caked child appears at her door, speaking a language no one in the valley knows, clutching a shard that hums like a trapped wasp. Astrid's beasts recoil from it. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Shard Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with fragments of the shard's visions. Touching it, Astrid sees a girl in an iron court, her soul being portioned out. The child says one word Astrid understands: sister. Emotional beat: horror and reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: The Warden's Question
chapters.summary: POV of Brammel, the valley warden, investigating rumors of magic at the valley's edge. He interviews Astrid, who lies well and hates it. Emotional beat: the walls of a safe life closing in.

chapters.title: Hunters at the Border
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Soul-hunters arrive at the ward's edge, unable to enter, patient as winter. Astrid realizes the shard is a beacon and the valley will not hold them forever. Emotional beat: the end of safety.

chapters.title: Crossing the Ward
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She and the child — named Wren — slip past the ward at night; Astrid's magic floods back like blood into a numb limb. The beasts beyond the valley answer her loudly, hungrily. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: The Outlaw Road
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On the mountain road they're caught by the Kettlebones, an outlaw band who trade in stolen court-tokens. Their leader, Sef, recognizes the shard and wants to sell it. Emotional beat: out of one trap into another.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Wolves
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid proves her worth by speaking peace between Sef's wolves and the band, buying passage instead of a cell. Wren begins mimicking Astrid's words. Emotional beat: grudging alliance; first warmth.

chapters.title: The River-God's Toll
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The river-god Vess demands a memory as ferry-toll. Astrid pays one of her mother, and only then understands her mother knew magic — and paid something enormous. Emotional beat: grief opening like a door.

chapters.title: The Scribe Who Fell
chapters.summary: POV of Ilex, a disgraced Undercourt scribe living in exile, who once recorded the sale of a Lockridge soul. He recognizes Astrid's name and, terrified, agrees to help — or so he claims. Emotional beat: guilt wearing a helpful face.

chapters.title: What Mother Bought
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Ilex reveals the truth: her mother sold her own soul to the court to buy Astrid's silence-gift and the valley's protection. Astrid's whole life was a purchase. Emotional beat: fury, then a terrible tenderness.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV of the Soulkeeper, the court's second throne, who senses the fragment approaching and orders the hunters to bring Astrid alive — her inheritance makes her useful. Emotional beat: cold, patient menace.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Ilex sells their route to the hunters to buy back his court standing. Sef's band scatters; Wren is taken. Astrid escapes with the shard and nothing else. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the choice to keep going anyway.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid finds Sef's broken band and, instead of begging, offers them the thing no court can: her testimony, beast-spoken, of every wrong the court's hunters committed. The outlaws become her army. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — lawlessness in service of justice.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The outlaws breach the mountain's root-doors using Ilex's stolen seals; Astrid walks into the Undercourt's antechambers, where sold souls murmur in the walls. Emotional beat: claustrophobic courage.

chapters.title: The Iron Court
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid stands before the thrones, offers the shard, her mother's debt, and her own voice for Wren and Wren's sister. The Soulkeeper accepts the voice — and demands more: her inheritance entire. Emotional beat: the bargain turning ravenous.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Walls
chapters.summary: POV of Wren, caged in the soul-vault, hearing Astrid's voice join the walls — and recognizing, in the Old Tongue, the words of unbinding the shard has been teaching them all along. Emotional beat: the smallest character carrying the largest hope.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, voiceless. As the court claims her inheritance, Wren speaks the binding words first: the shard shatters, the sister's soul flies free, and every sold soul in the court wakes. Emotional beat: triumphant reversal — the child out-bargains the throne.

chapters.title: The Mountain's Anger
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The collapsing court turns on them; Sef's outlaws hold the root-doors while Astrid, mute, calls every beast of the mountain to carry them out. Ilex stays behind, choosing penance. Emotional beat: sacrifice and escape at a dead run.

chapters.title: Homecoming Without Words
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid and Wren return to Hollowvale; the ward, no longer fed by her mother's soul, flickers and opens. Brammel must choose between the law and the truth Astrid cannot speak. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning.

chapters.title: What the Beasts Said
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The valley's beasts gather and speak for her — her history, her mother's sacrifice, the court's crimes — and the valley chooses to believe. Wren's sister, restored, chooses to stay. Emotional beat: community as absolution.

chapters.title: The Open Valley
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, final. Astrid plants a garden over her mother's unmarked grave, teaches Wren the valley's names for things, and walks past the ward's edge without fear — the beasts' voices still with her, and her own silence full rather than empty. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed — not a debt paid, but a door opened.
